title: Update media resource fetch to identify top-level self-fetch for blob URLs
body: Updates the media resource fetch algorithm to calculate when a top-level self-fetch might be occurring for blob URLs, which is a case where blob URL partitioning would be bypassed. For more info see: https://github.com/w3c/FileAPI/issues/210 - [x] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed): * Implemented in Chromium: https://crbug.com/426787402 * WebKit - [x] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at: * I don't think this case is testable via WPTs... You'd need some way to navigate to a blob URL that has a media mime type and that was created in a third-party context (resulting in the creation of a first-party [media document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#read-media)), and then be able to inspect the state of that document to see whether the video element played successfully. We enforce no-opener on cross-top-level-site blob URL navigations, so there's no handle to the new page, and we can't otherwise inspect it's state or execute code in it's context AFAIK. For testing Chrome's implementation we have [a browser test](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/6656174/8/content/browser/blob_storage/blob_url_browsertest.cc) that can run Javascript in the newly opened window - [x] [Implementation bugs](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) are filed: * Chromium: https://crbug.com/426787402 * Gecko: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2000324 * WebKit: https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=302558 * Deno (only for timers, structured clone, base64 utils, channel messaging, module resolution, web workers, and web storage): N/A since Deno does not partition storage or more generally implement the same-origin policy: https://docs.deno.com/runtime/reference/web_platform_apis/#spec-deviations * Node.js (only for timers, structured clone, base64 utils, channel messaging, and module resolution): N/A - [x] Corresponding [HTML AAM](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/) & [ARIA in HTML](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/) issues & PRs: N/A - [x] [MDN issue](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) is filed: https://github.com/mdn/mdn/issues/773 - [x] The top of this comment includes a [clear commit message](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/COMMITTING.md) to use.
